termsGate.title: Experiment Lab, Terms and Privacy
termsGate.para: ResoPulse is a closed-loop in-vitro electroporation digital twin. Every prediction is a simulator output, every calibration is your bench data. It is not a medical device and must not be used for clinical diagnostics or human treatment.
termsGate.li1: All algorithms, physics models, and source code are the exclusive property of Tomer Preis and protected by copyright.
termsGate.li2: You may not reverse-engineer, clone, or use this tool to build competing software.
termsGate.li3: Biophysical parameters are approximations, real-world results may vary.
termsGate.li4: Tomer Preis assumes no liability for experimental outcomes or laboratory decisions.

signIn.cardDesc: Continue your closed-loop session, residuals and all
signIn.brandSub: Predict with peer-reviewed physics. Calibrate with your measured bench outcomes. Let the loop close between simulator and cuvette.
signIn.tipClosedLoop: Closed-Loop Digital Twin Log your bench outcomes (target/healthy lysis, viability, PI, qPCR, temperature) and the simulator calibrates against them on every run. Drift, Moderate, and Strong tiers score how closely predictions match your cuvette.
signIn.tipSchwan: Schwan EP Model Computes transmembrane voltage Vm(f) using the Schwan equation for spherical cells. Peak Vm of 1.5 V is achievable at DC or sub-fc frequencies for typical mammalian cells.
signIn.tipCalibration: Per-cell σᵢ calibration A scalar multiplier fit to your measured bench data corrects the simulator's internal conductivity assumption per cell line. Clamped to a plausibility band; the chart shows mean residual tightening over time.
signIn.tipActiveLearn: Active-learning suggestions The Suggest Next button picks the (frequency, field) point farthest from your logged conditions in log-space, so the next bench run samples a region your data has not yet covered.
signIn.tipAiOptimizer: AI Protocol Optimizer XGBoost trained on your rated outcomes recommends a full protocol (frequency, field, duty cycle, pulse width, waveform). Falls back to the Schwan physics baseline when fewer than 20 rated outcomes are on file.
